name: i2spec2026k
source: E. J. Salumbides, K. S. E. Eikema, W. Ubachs, U. Hollenstein, H. Knöckel, E. Tiemann, Eur. Phys. J. D 47, 171 (2008), Table 1
units: cm^-1 and Angstrom; C_n in cm^-1 Angstrom^n
notes: Outer branch V = De - sum C_n/R^n - A_O exp(-B_O (R - R_O)) (paper eq. 4). BOC: alpha(R) = (mu_ref/mu) (2Rm/(R+Rm)) sum alpha_i X^i; V_corr = (1 - mu_ref/mu) (2Rm/(R+Rm))^l sum v_i X^i with l = 5. De and C_n from Gerstenkorn, Luc & Le Roy 1991, Gerstenkorn, Luc & Amiot 1985 (B) and Bacis, Cerny & Martin 1986 (X). Turning points covered by data: B 2.650-4.589 A, X 2.427-3.079 A. i2spec2026a: the hannover2008 potentials with the changes listed under 'changes'. The hyperfine table (i2spec.hfs_table) and the MLR trial potentials (data/potentials/) are separate. i2spec2026c carries measured level corrections for the NIR and the visible (see changes).

changes.what: B state adiabatic Born-Oppenheimer correction, constant term
changes.why: Every 129I2 line in the BIPM 612 and 633 nm tables sits 7-14 MHz above the published model and 127I129I 4.6 MHz below 129I2, each with sub-MHz scatter inside the line. A constant in V_ad enters the levels as (1 - mu_127/mu) V_ad0: 0.0155 for 129I2, 0.0085 for 127I129I, so one number moves both by the right ratio. Fitted to the 124 isotopologue rows that constrain the potentials (prototypes/bo_refit.py): rms 7.06 -> 2.36 MHz against a data floor of 1.1-1.2 MHz. A slope or an alpha term reaches 1.4 MHz but with degenerate, run-dependent values from seven independent numbers, so only the constant is adopted. R(113) 14-4 stays +5.1 MHz.

changes.what: measured level corrections for 127I2 in the near infrared: X v'' = 11-17 and B v' = 1-3, 5, 7
changes.why: The potentials miss the comb-referenced NIR lines (liao2010a, bodermann2000a, bodermann1998b, reinhardt2007a, cornish2000a; 71 lines, 0.02-0.3 MHz) by 3.0 MHz rms with a shape that is smooth in J within each band. Polynomials in J(J+1) per level, fitted as a robust ridge regression on the residuals (prototypes/nir_corrections.py), bring them to 0.25 MHz in-sample and 0.4 MHz median leave-one-line-out. IodineSpec5 covers the same range with a local Dunham model fitted to the same data. δB(v'=0) = 0 by convention; the corrections apply to 127I2 only and are trusted within 15 in J of the measured range (lookup.uncertainty).

changes.what: level corrections extended from the near infrared to every comb-referenced 127I2 line with v' <= 43, v'' <= 17
changes.why: The residual structure of the default against the precise sets is level-shaped: nishiyama2024a is a pure +5.57 MHz offset of B v' = 39 (scatter 0.11), bipm2012a a set of per-v' offsets at v' = 32-37 (-2 to +4 MHz), bipm2005a a -1.4 MHz offset of B v' = 43. The same polynomial-per-level fit as the NIR corrections, on all 839 127I2 position rows (605 touching a corrected level), takes the comb-referenced sets to 0.02-0.3 MHz in-sample and 0.1-0.8 MHz leave-one-line-out (prototypes/level_corrections_fit.py). A level's parameters come only from lines measured to <= 0.3 MHz; each level carries its held-out rms into lookup.uncertainty.

changes.what: extended-range potentials: the MLR pair mlr_x_2026c / mlr_b_2026c supplies the X levels from v'' = 18 and the B levels from v' = 44 up
changes.why: The published curves are fitted to v'' <= 17 and v' <= 43 and fail beyond: +7.8 cm-1 at v'' = 48, -21 cm-1 at v'' = 54, 2.2 cm-1 against the atlas at v' = 58, 25 GHz on matsunaga2024a. The MLR pair (docs/design/mlr-x.md) is 10^2-10^4 better there and tracks Martin 1986's X levels to 0.1-0.3 GHz through the unmeasured gap (docs/research/iodinespec5.md). Inside the published range the two are equivalent after level corrections (held-out 1.68 vs 1.70 MHz over 605 rows) and the published curves stay, so every level comes from the model that is validated there.

changes.what: level corrections refitted on the hybrid, now reaching v' <= 50 and v'' <= 54
changes.why: Same fit as i2spec2026c's, with the base the hybrid set and the range extended: yoshiki2023a 3.3 -> 0.6 MHz, matsunaga2024a 12.5 -> 2.0; B v' = 44 and 45 validated at 0.7 MHz held out. The v'' = 48-54 sets stay at 6-19 MHz, which is the X hyperfine model there, not the levels.

changes.what: a local correction for the NIR bands v' = 0 -> v'' = 12-17, on top of the unchanged level corrections
changes.why: After the level corrections the comb-referenced NIR lines are R-high / P-low at the same J'' (liao2010a R(106) 0-13 +0.70, R(100) 0-12 +0.59, P(82) 0-13 -0.39 MHz), which needs a J'-dependence of B v' = 0. Put on the levels, that moves 0-9/0-10 by +13 MHz at J = 100 and the v' >= 1 bands to v'' = 11-17 by up to -130 MHz with nothing measured there, so it is applied to the lines of these bands only, within 15 in J'' of the data at each v'' - the confinement IodineSpec5's local NIR model has. Liao 2010 enters with its +114 kHz pressure shift. liao2010a 0.35 -> 0.074 MHz in-sample (0.22 held out); all 60 precise NIR rows 0.27 -> 0.25 held out, worst 0.72 MHz. Nothing outside the bands moves. prototypes/nir_band_fit.py --degree=3,2,3 --floor=0.05

changes.what: Bodermann's 1998 thesis data (bodermann1998c) added: level corrections and NIR band correction refitted
changes.why: Bodermann's thesis (Hannover 1998, bodermann1998c) supplies the difference frequencies behind the Hannover NIR local model: 54 rows, 52 of them beats between lines of 0-12..0-17 and 1-14 at 5-45 kHz, never published. Level corrections refitted with them (bodermann2000a held out 4.99 -> 0.51 MHz, reinhardt2007a 4.53 -> 0.63), then the band correction on top, chosen by the same rule as i2spec2026e over a wider grid: (L,K,KB) = (5,3,4), floor 0.1, prior 50 MHz. liao2010a 0.119 MHz raw (IodineSpec5 0.138), 0.027 with its 114 kHz shift, 0.053 held out; all 108 precise NIR rows 0.326 -> 0.132 held out (median 0.026, worst 0.67). prototypes/nir_band_fit.py --parameters=i2spec2026f --degree=5,3,4 --floor=0.1 --prior=50

changes.what: X v'' = 18-25 corrected from the Orsay atlas part I (Gerstenkorn, Verges & Chevillard 1982, 4 826 lines at 790 C)
changes.why: The first measurement of the X state above v'' = 17 in this project. 3 700 atlas lines assigned against a model list thinned to the atlas's density (4 % expected by chance; 1 349 R/P pairs from shared upper levels agree to 41 MHz median). Fitted with a pure scale calibration, +24 ppb, as the atlas's own page IV prescribes, anchored on v'' <= 17 lines inside the comb-measured J ranges, and a linear J(J+1) correction per level: dX from -16 MHz (v'' = 18) to -57 MHz (v'' = 24), -81 at v'' = 25. v' = 0, 1, 2 sub-samples of a level agree to ~15 MHz; freeing the upper levels' J-dependence changes nothing. Level uncertainty 15-45 MHz, down from 300. prototypes/orsay_assign.py, orsay_fit.py --free=18-25 --maxdeg=1

changes.what: extended-range X refitted to the Orsay-atlas levels (mlr_x_2026d)
changes.why: mlr_x_2026c refitted to the atlas-corrected levels v''=18-25, anchored on its own v''<=17 levels, the emission levels v''=48,53,54 and the long-range priors: atlas levels 33 -> 16.5 MHz rms; leave-one-level-out predicts every v''=18-25 level better than 2026c did and within its uncertainty (7-38 MHz). Moves v''=26-47 by up to -100 MHz (peak v''~34). Corrections re-expressed on the new potential so the covered levels are unchanged. prototypes/mlr_x_atlas.py

changes.what: level-correction curvature terms held at the edge of their measured J range
changes.why: Beyond coverage +- 15 the quadratic and cubic terms of a level correction are fitted scatter, and extrapolated they moved lines by tens of MHz (1-13 +57, 1-14 -35 MHz at J'' = 300). Holding the whole polynomial constant was tried first and is wrong: velchev1998a's B v' = 16 lines at J' = 117-138, beyond the J' <= 78 the correction was fitted on, are -0.2 to -0.9 MHz extrapolated and -2 to -4 MHz clamped. So the constant and J(J+1) terms keep extrapolating and only the curvature is held. No measured data set moves.

changes.what: B level corrections refitted with seven more comb-referenced data sets
changes.why: ikeda2022a (514 nm, v' = 45, 46, 48), cheng2019a (534 nm, v' = 31), shie2013a (535 nm, v' = 30), hsiao2013a (548 nm, v' = 24), zhang2009a (560 nm, v' = 20, 23), yang2011a (561 nm, v' = 22-24) and edwards1999a (633 nm, v' = 6): 174 rows, whose absolute frequencies sat 1-5 MHz from i2spec2026i in the visible and 26 MHz at v' = 48. The same fit and degree rule as level_corrections_2026c-h (prototypes/level_corrections_fit.py --base=i2spec2026d --extended), which reproduces the B section of 2026h to 1e-6 MHz without the new sets; B v' = 20, 23, 24, 30, 31 and 48 are newly corrected, v' = 22, 45, 46 refitted. v' = 24 has two lines, J' = 27 and 131, 7 MHz apart, so its held-out figure is 7 MHz. X, band and Orsay sections unchanged.

changes.what: B to the dissociation limit: the B MLR refitted with the Orsay atlas Partie IV (mlr_b_2026d), and B v' = 51-79 corrected level by level from the atlas and the comb lines there
changes.why: i2spec2026j's B MLR was fitted to v' <= 62 and missed the atlas by 3-390 GHz above v' = 58, and bound nothing above v' = 75. 2 009 unblended atlas lines (Gerstenkorn & Luc 1983, v' = 51-79) refit it with a long-range centrifugal constant q_far; corrections re-fitted for v' = 44-50 on the new potential; v' = 51-79 corrected from the atlas with its offset (+119 MHz) fixed by R(26) 62-0, P(40) 52-0 and P(52) 53-0. prototypes/mlr_b_dissociation.py, prototypes/orsay4_fit.py; docs/research/orsay-atlas-19700-20035.md
